ai.literal: Because rain, persisting, sustains the world by coming, it is fit to be understood as nectar itself.
ai.translation: Since rain pours down continuously and sustains the world, it should be understood as the very nectar of life.
ai.modern: மழை தொடர்ந்து பெய்து உலகத்தைக் காத்து வருவதால், அதுவே அமிழ்தம் என்று உணரத்தக்கது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of rain by comparing it to 'amiḻtam', the mythical nectar of immortality. The word 'vān' refers to the sky, but here it specifically denotes the rain that falls from it. Because rain falls regularly and sustains all living beings, it acts as the ultimate life-giver. The poet suggests that we must realize ('uṇaraṟ pāṟṟu') that rain is not just water, but the very source of existence that keeps the world alive.

ai.literal: To those who eat, producing foods that are food, and to those who eat, itself becoming food, is rain.
ai.translation: Rain produces good food for those who eat, and itself becomes food for them as well.
ai.modern: உண்பவர்களுக்கு நல்ல உணவுகளை உண்டாக்கித் தருவதோடு, உண்பவர்களுக்குத் தானும் ஓர் உணவாக இருப்பது மழையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the dual role of rain in sustaining life through a masterful play on the word 'tuppu' (meaning food or enjoyment). First, rain acts as the source that enables agriculture and produces various foods for living beings to consume. Second, water itself is an essential, direct food (drink) without which life cannot survive. By repeating variations of 'tuppu', the poet emphasizes that rain is both the creator of sustenance and sustenance itself.

words.gloss: the sky (or rain from the sky)

ai.literal: If the sky, failing, deceives, within the vast-watered great world, abiding inside, hunger will torment.
ai.translation: If the heavens fail and dry up, hunger will abide within and torment this great world, even though it is surrounded by the vast ocean.
ai.modern: மழை பெய்யாமல் பொய்த்துப் போனால், பரந்த கடலால் சூழப்பட்ட இப்பெரிய உலகத்தில் பசி நிலைபெற்று உயிர்களைத் துன்புறுத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of rain for survival. The poet contrasts the vast ocean ('விரிநீர்') surrounding the earth with the rain from the sky ('விண்'). Although the world is surrounded by abundant water, ocean water cannot sustain life or grow food. If the clouds fail ('பொய்ப்பின்') to bring rain, hunger ('பசி') will establish itself ('உள்நின்று') and torment ('உடற்றும்') all living beings on this great earth.

ai.literal: With the plough, they will not plough, the farmers, if the bounty called rain diminishes in its abundance.
ai.translation: Farmers will not plough their fields with oxen if the abundance of the bounty called rain diminishes.
ai.modern: மழை என்று சொல்லப்படும் வருவாயின் வளம் குறைந்தால், உழவர்கள் ஏரைக் கொண்டு உழவு செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute dependency of agriculture on rainfall. The poet states that if the abundance of the bounty known as rain diminishes, even the farmers, whose primary duty is to cultivate, will not be able to plough their fields. The word 'vārī' refers to the bounty or yield of water that rain provides, and 'kāl' functions here as a conditional marker meaning 'when' or 'if'. Without this heavenly resource, all agricultural activity comes to a standstill.

words.gloss: right there / at that very moment

parts.gloss: that which lifts up / restores (with poetic lengthening)

ai.literal: That which ruins, and to those who are ruined as a support right there that which lifts up, all is rain.
ai.translation: Rain is that which ruins; and it is also that which, acting as a support, lifts up and restores those who are ruined.
ai.modern: மழை பெய்யாமல் மக்களைக் கெடுப்பதும், வறுமையால் கெட்டுப்போனவர்களுக்குத் துணையாக இருந்து பெய்து அவர்களைக் காப்பதும் எல்லாமே மழைதான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute power of rain over human life. By withholding itself, rain has the power to destroy livelihoods and cause ruin. Conversely, by falling at the right moment, it acts as a support to revive and lift up those who have been ruined by drought. The poet uses the poetic lengthening (alapedai) in 'கெடுப்பதூஉம்' and 'எடுப்பதூஉம்' to emphasize these two contrasting, yet equally powerful, actions of the rain.

ai.literal: If a drop of the sky falls except, then, right there, green grass's tip to see is rare.
ai.translation: Unless drops of rain fall from the sky, it is impossible to see even the tip of a single blade of green grass.
ai.modern: வானத்திலிருந்து மழைத்துளி விழுந்தால் ஒழிய, அந்த இடத்திலே ஒரு பச்சைப் புல்லின் நுனியைக் கூடக் காண்பது அரிதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of rain for terrestrial life by focusing on its simplest form: grass. The poet states that without rain falling from the sky (விசும்பின் துளி), one cannot even see the tip (தலை) of a blade of green grass (பசும்புல்). The word 'தலை' (literally 'head') is used here to denote the very first shoot or tip of the grass that emerges from the soil. By showing that even the humblest and most resilient plant cannot sprout without rain, the couplet emphasizes that all life on earth is entirely dependent on water from above.

ai.literal: Even the vast ocean its own abundance will diminish, if the cloud, having condensed, itself without giving becomes.
ai.translation: Even the vast ocean's own abundance will diminish, if the cloud, having drawn its water, fails to give it back as rain.
ai.modern: மேகமானது கடலிலிருந்து நீரை முகந்து கொண்டு சென்று, மீண்டும் மழையாகப் பொழியாமல் போனால், பரந்த கடலும் தன் வளம் குன்றிப் போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully illustrates the water cycle and the concept of mutual dependence in nature. The word 'நீர்மை' refers to the ocean's inherent quality of abundance, wealth, and life-supporting nature. The poet explains that even the immense ocean, which seems to have an inexhaustible supply of water, will lose its richness and shrink if the clouds ('எழிலி') do not return the water they took. It teaches us that no matter how vast one's resources are, they will eventually deplete without the cycle of giving and receiving.

ai.literal: With grand festivals, daily worship will not happen, if the sky dries up, even for the heavenly beings, here.
ai.translation: If the heavens dry up, neither grand festivals nor daily worship will be offered here in this world, even to the heavenly gods.
ai.modern: வானம் மழை தராமல் வறண்டு போனால், இவ்வுலகில் தேவர்களுக்கும் கூடச் சிறப்பு வழிபாடுகளும் தினசரி பூசைகளும் நடைபெறாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute dependency of all religious rituals on rain. The author states that if the sky fails to pour rain, even the gods in heaven will not receive their grand festivals or daily offerings from the people on earth. The word 'வறக்குமேல்' combines 'வறக்கும்' (dries up) and 'ஏல்' (if) to set the condition of drought. The particle 'உம்' in 'வானோர்க்கும்' emphasizes that even the divine beings, who are otherwise exalted, lose their worship when the earth lacks water.

ai.literal: Charity and penance, both of these will not endure in the vast world, if the sky does not give (rain).
ai.translation: If the heavens do not pour down rain, neither charity nor penance will endure in this vast world.
ai.modern: வானம் மழையைத் தராவிட்டால், இந்தப் பரந்த உலகத்தில் தானமும் தவமும் ஆகிய இரண்டும் நிலைபெற்று இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute dependence of human moral and spiritual life on rain. The poet states that if the sky fails to give rain, the two fundamental virtues of human society—charity (giving to others) and penance (self-discipline)—will cease to exist in this vast world. Without rain, there is no food or prosperity, making charity impossible; and without basic survival, the mental peace and stability required for spiritual penance are lost. Thus, rain is shown as the essential foundation for both social duty and spiritual practice.

ai.literal: If the world cannot exist without water, for anyone, righteous conduct cannot exist without rain.
ai.translation: If the world cannot exist without water, then righteous conduct cannot exist for anyone without rain.
ai.modern: நீர் இல்லாமல் உலகம் இயங்காது என்றால், மழை இல்லாமல் எவருக்கும் ஒழுக்கமான வாழ்க்கை அமையாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on the importance of rain by linking physical survival with moral order. The poet argues that just as the physical world cannot function without water, human society cannot maintain its moral and righteous conduct without rain. Rain brings the prosperity and sustenance required for people to practice virtues and duties. Without the life-giving rain, the very foundation of human ethics and orderly life collapses.
